content: Nevirapine is a medication prescribed to address specific health needs, particularly in the treatment of HIV. Common side effects may include tiredness, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. In rare cases, drowsiness may occur. It is also possible to notice the empty shell of the extended-release tablet in your stool, which is normal and not a cause for concern. This medication is prescribed because your doctor has determined that its benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens during treatment, it may begin to combat pre-existing infections, which could cause symptoms of those infections to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune response may occur, potentially leading to symptoms. These reactions can happen at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or even months later. Nevirapine commonly causes a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it is important to monitor for rare rashes that may indicate a severe reaction. Changes in body fat distribution may also occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas or decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are not fully understood. Severe allergic reactions to nevirapine are rare but require immediate medical attention if they occur. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the United States, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, contact your doctor for guidance. Before taking nevirapine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Rarely, this medication may cause drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can increase drowsiness, so avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, nevirapine should only be used when clearly necessary. HIV treatment, including nevirapine, can reduce the risk of transmitting the virus to your baby. However, this medication does pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor for advice. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications, such as rifamycins (e.g., rifampin), may affect how nevirapine is removed from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Nevirapine can also speed up the removal of other medications, which may impact their effectiveness. Do not use prednisone to prevent a rash, as it may increase the risk of developing a rash during the first six weeks of nevirapine treatment. Additionally, this medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In the event of an overdose, if someone experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
